title: 2-week React Native skill test plan
summary: Prepare for a timed React Native skill test: 17 lessons, 16 runnable TypeScript exercises checked in the browser, a React Native flashcard deck and two runs of the timed simulator. About 1–1.5 hours a day.

rhythm.text: Read one or two lessons, try every gotcha before opening its answer, then make the exercises pass without looking at the hints first.
Timed practice or a full test, then review: reread the lessons for weak topics and clear due flashcards.

rules: Know which thread does the work: JavaScript, UI or native.
Use virtualised lists with stable keys for anything long or unbounded.
Every subscription, listener and timer is cleaned up when its screen goes away.
Keep secrets in the secure store, and treat the network as unreliable.
Keep the timer honest in practice runs: no notes and no pausing.

typescript: Model actions as a discriminated union so the reducer switch is checked: type Action = { type: 'push'; route: Route } | { type: 'pop' }.
Type navigation params per screen with a map: type Params = { Order: { id: string } }.
Return new objects from reducers and mark state readonly to catch mutation.
Catch errors as unknown and narrow with instanceof Error before reading message.
Use generics for reusable helpers such as caches and queues: class Cache<T>.

phases.title: Components, navigation and data
phases.check: Without notes, explain how FlatList virtualises and how a stack navigator keeps screens, and write a navigation stack reducer.

phases.title: Production apps and the test
phases.check: Score 70% or more in every topic of the timed simulator, and pass both coding tasks within the time limit.

weeks.title: Components, lists, navigation, architecture and state
weeks.focus: Core components and flexbox, virtualised lists, stack navigation and deep links, platform differences, the new architecture, native modules and app state. Finish with a timed practice run.

tip.typescript: Type reducer actions as a discriminated union and screen params as a map, so mistakes show up before you run the tests.
